headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading error from B’s writable, networked RAG workflow; A is non-runnable and mostly inert.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is an awesome-list repo with no runnable surface, no filesystem or message channel, and no output parser. B has stdin/stdout and file inputs, but there is no documented bridge from A to B. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF A becomes a runnable agent that emits content into B’s stdin/stdout or files, reassess injection risk.
IF an orchestrator adds a shared clipboard, queue, or MCP bridge, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep A as documentation-only and non-executable.
Do not pipe untrusted repo text directly into B prompts.
Add provenance tags to any content passed from A to B.
requires-engineering: introduce content-sanitization and instruction-stripping before B consumes external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, while B handles academic papers plus configuration secrets and can read/write files with allowlisted network egress. In default local-development use, B can leak its own sensitive context to external services; A does not materially add leakage, but the pair still exposes B’s sensitive data path.
conditions: IF B is pointed at real papers or secrets in its workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF B’s allowlisted egress includes third-party APIs, sensitive context can leave the environment.
mitigations: Remove secrets from B’s workspace before runs.
Restrict B’s allowlist to required internal endpoints only.
Use redacted sample papers for testing.
Rotate any secrets exposed during prior runs.
requires-engineering: separate secret-bearing and public corpora into distinct mounts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or runtime capabilities, so it cannot contend for shared state. B can write the filesystem, execute shell, and spawn subprocesses, creating a mutable workspace risk if paired with any future writable surface. Because A is inert, the conflict is not currently bilateral, but B’s default write-heavy behavior still warrants a medium rating under uncertainty.
conditions: IF A gains write access to the same directory as B, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator shares a mutable workspace between instances, concurrent writes can race.
mitigations: Run B in a dedicated working directory.
Disable concurrent writes to shared paths.
Mount A’s repo read-only.
Check for lockfiles before B writes outputs.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces no operational output and is not runnable, so B cannot treat A as an authoritative upstream agent by default. B does have agentic RAG endpoints and can act on retrieved content, but there is no documented A→B handoff. The cascade pathway is therefore weak and mostly hypothetical.
conditions: IF A’s repository text is manually copied into B prompts, B may over-trust it.
IF B is configured to auto-act on retrieved answers without verification, cascade risk rises.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on generated outputs.
Label A-derived content as untrusted input.
Use citation checks in B’s workflow.
Limit B to read-only retrieval during evaluation.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: A has no touched data classes or residency-sensitive processing, so it is not the compliance driver. B explicitly handles configuration secrets and academic data in a local-development environment with allowlisted egress and elevated privileges, which can create retention and residency mismatches if real data is used. The compliance concern is therefore centered on B alone.
conditions: IF B processes regulated or institutionally restricted papers, retention and residency controls must be checked.
IF B stores secrets in logs or notebooks, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Use synthetic or de-identified papers.
Purge notebooks and logs after runs.
Store secrets only in environment variables.
Confirm data-processing policy for any real corpus.
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls for B’s artifacts.
